Updates `playwright` from 1.63.0 to 1.64.0
Release notes

Sourced from playwright's releases.

v1.64.0

🧰 WebMCP

New page.webmcp and frame.webmcp give access to the tools that a page registers through the experimental WebMCP browser API, so you can test them like any other part of your app:

const browser = await chromium.launch({ args: ['--enable-features=WebMCP'] });
const page = await browser.newPage();
await page.goto('https://example.com');

for (const tool of await page.webmcp.tools())
console.log(tool.name, tool.description);


const result = await page.webmcp.callTool('add', { a: 2, b: 40 });
console.log(result.content[0].text); // "42"

Playwright MCP also supports WebMCP by default, with page-defined tools offered to the agent as webmcp_<tool>. Pass --no-webmcp to opt out.

playwright-cli exposes them as well:

playwright-cli webmcp-list
playwright-cli webmcp-call search_catalog --params '{"query":"cats"}'

🎬 Better videos

Videos can now be recorded at a custom frame rate, and the decorations for actions are styled with plain CSS:

// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
use: {
video: {
mode: 'on',
size: { width: 1920, height: 1080 },
fps: 60,
show: {
actions: {
style: {
point: 'width: 20px; height: 20px; border-radius: 50%; background: red',
highlight: 'outline: 2px solid #333; background: rgba(0, 128, 255, .15)',
title: 'font-size: 16px',
},
},
},
},
</tr></table>

... (truncated)

Bumps [@hyzyla/pdfium](https://github.com/hyzyla/pdfium) from 2.1.13 to 3.0.0.
Release notes

Sourced from @​hyzyla/pdfium's releases.

v3.0.0

Breaking changes

  • Node.js 22 or newer is required.
  • @hyzyla/pdfium/browser/base64 is now @hyzyla/pdfium/inline. It also runs in Node.js, which makes it the easiest option when a bundler leaves pdfium.wasm behind (Next.js, esbuild and similar).
  • Files under dist/ can no longer be imported directly. Use the package entry points. @hyzyla/pdfium/pdfium.wasm is still exported.
  • The "BGRA" color space is now called "RGBA", which matches the bytes it always returned. "BGRA" still works as a deprecated alias.
  • The CDN entry no longer exposes PDFiumLibrary._cache.
  • page.render() no longer closes the page, so you can render it again or read its text afterwards. Pages stay loaded until you call the new page.close() or destroy the document, so close pages you're done with when working through a large document. Worker pages have close() too.

New

  • Text objects have a getText() method, for the text of a single object on the page.

Fixes

  • require() users get CommonJS type declarations (.d.cts).
  • The instantiateWasm option has the right type, and wasmBinary accepts a Uint8Array or Node.js Buffer.
  • init() returns an instance of the class you imported.
  • The worker no longer hangs when the wasm fails to load, and no longer detaches the rest of a buffer when you pass part of it.
  • Rendering image objects no longer leaks memory.
  • The CDN entry downloads the wasm once and reports failed downloads clearly.
  • Empty or detached PDF data, and a missing wasm option outside Node.js, now produce clear errors.
  • Bundlers no longer copy an unused pdfium.wasm into apps that use the CDN or inline entry.
  • The Node.js build no longer fails with createRequire is not a function in older webpack versions, like the one inside Next.js.
  • @hyzyla/pdfium/package.json is exported.
  • PDFium is updated from 7243 to 8046d. Rendered images may not match 2.x pixel for pixel.
Commits
  • c60c75d Document the Electron setup
  • 5df6045 Document text object extraction
  • d95d15e Add getText to text objects
  • 0690f97 Fix the raw image data docs
  • c4724a9 Test that raw DCTDecode image data is the JPEG file
  • 5b258d3 Document the Next.js setup
  • 3245f56 Test the Node.js entry bundled with webpack
  • e5f23c3 Fix createRequire in older webpack runtimes
  • 40a76b6 Test rendering pages concurrently
  • 0428a77 Release 3.0.0
  • Additional commits viewable in compare view

Bumps [@rgrove/parse-xml](https://github.com/rgrove/parse-xml) from 4.2.3 to 5.0.0.
Release notes

Sourced from @​rgrove/parse-xml's releases.

v5.0.0

parse-xml is now an ES module. The API is completely unchanged, but the package format and the minimum supported Node.js version have changed. See below for details.

Breaking Changes

  • parse-xml is now an ES module. The package sets "type": "module" and ships ESM rather than CommonJS.

    If you already use import, you don't need to change anything:

    import { parseXml } from '@rgrove/parse-xml';

    Using require() also still works in Node.js 22+ thanks to require(esm):

    const { parseXml } = require('@rgrove/parse-xml');

    There are two cases that will require a change: bundlers or runtimes that can't resolve ESM at all will no longer work, and if your own project is CommonJS and written in TypeScript, you'll need TypeScript 5.8 or later with "module": "nodenext". Older versions of TypeScript and configs using "module": "node16" don't support require(esm) and will report an error.

  • Node.js 22.12.0 is now the minimum supported version (up from 14.0.0, which hadn't actually been tested in some time).

  • The package now has an exports map, so only its public API can be imported. The root entry and the Xml* node classes are unaffected:

    import { parseXml, XmlElement } from '@rgrove/parse-xml';
import { XmlElement } from '@rgrove/parse-xml/dist/lib/XmlElement.js';

    But Parser, StringScanner, syntax, and types are no longer importable. These were never documented as public or exported from the package's entry point so this is unlikely to affect most people.

  • The browser bundle at dist/browser.js is now ESM rather than CommonJS. This is the file bundlers pick up via the browser field, so it should be transparent. As an added bonus, it's also 1.1 KB smaller now.

    The minified global bundle at dist/global.min.js is unchanged, so loading parse-xml from a CDN with a <script> element and using the parseXml global works exactly as before.

Other Changes

  • The published npm package is about 40% smaller (48 KB packed, down from 82 KB in 4.2.3) because it no longer includes unnecessary sourcemaps that are only useful during development.

Updates `playwright` from 1.63.0 to 1.64.0
Release notes

Sourced from playwright's releases.

v1.64.0

🧰 WebMCP

New page.webmcp and frame.webmcp give access to the tools that a page registers through the experimental WebMCP browser API, so you can test them like any other part of your app:

const browser = await chromium.launch({ args: ['--enable-features=WebMCP'] });
const page = await browser.newPage();
await page.goto('https://example.com');

for (const tool of await page.webmcp.tools())
console.log(tool.name, tool.description);


const result = await page.webmcp.callTool('add', { a: 2, b: 40 });
console.log(result.content[0].text); // "42"

Playwright MCP also supports WebMCP by default, with page-defined tools offered to the agent as webmcp_<tool>. Pass --no-webmcp to opt out.

playwright-cli exposes them as well:

playwright-cli webmcp-list
playwright-cli webmcp-call search_catalog --params '{"query":"cats"}'

🎬 Better videos

Videos can now be recorded at a custom frame rate, and the decorations for actions are styled with plain CSS:

// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
use: {
video: {
mode: 'on',
size: { width: 1920, height: 1080 },
fps: 60,
show: {
actions: {
style: {
point: 'width: 20px; height: 20px; border-radius: 50%; background: red',
highlight: 'outline: 2px solid #333; background: rgba(0, 128, 255, .15)',
title: 'font-size: 16px',
},
},
},
},
</tr></table>
